claims.text: The starting material is a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix.
A high-entropy-alloy coating is applied as an interface modification.
High-entropy-alloy interface coatings can reduce phase separation in W–Cu composites.
High-entropy-alloy interface coatings can reduce interfacial void formation in W–Cu composites.
The coating improves bonding at the W–Cu interface.
Improved interfacial bonding and reduced void formation increase the thermal conductivity of the W–Cu composite.
A high-entropy-alloy-coated W–Cu composite will have higher thermal conductivity than an untreated W–Cu composite.
The predicted improvement applies under heat-transfer conditions relevant to W-based plasma-facing-material/Cu-based cooling-component joints.
The predicted improvement applies under irradiation conditions relevant to W-based plasma-facing-material/Cu-based cooling-component joints.
Applicability is limited by processing and service conditions, although no quantitative boundaries are specified.
The magnitude of any thermal-conductivity improvement is uncertain and requires experimentation.
Failure of the coated composite to show a statistically significant thermal-conductivity improvement over the untreated control would falsify the hypothesis.
